note: He clears four of the five criteria. Successful is a qualified match rather than a clean one - he runs an electrical department building ships and owns and operates a sawmill, so he is a business owner in the literal sense, but a tradesman-manager with a side business is not what 'business owner, physician or equivalent' is reaching for. Health is genuinely the neglected area and not a crisis: he already fixed the crisis himself eighteen months ago, going from 240 lb to 185 and quitting alcohol, and what has slipped since is training and mobility. Good-to-great is explicit, and the rep categorised him on the call as 'either average or good already, but they're trying to get to the next level'. He is plainly not deconditioned. The miss is income, and it is unusual and worth separating from the batch's other income failures: this is not a man who cannot afford $6,000 in principle - he wanted to pay in full up front, rejected the cheaper tier, and rejected financing because he dislikes monthly payments. He simply cannot know what he has until a divorce settlement completes, five days after the fact. The stated ICP has no way to represent a qualified buyer in a temporary legal freeze, so an income screen would drop him permanently for a condition that expires in about a week. That makes him the best argument in the batch for tracking a buying window rather than a binary income gate.
